groups.reason: The legacy headless fixture assumes a render camera raises the production 32-block player baseline to 64 blocks and then shares ordered static state across tests. The v2 scenario proves streaming and revisions without that render dependency.

These order-dependent scripts predate lifecycle generations and authoritative body revisions. The v2 scenario creates deterministic entities and verifies stale-generation rejection, observer convergence, late join, reconnect, faults, and reload.

The legacy assertion depends on an obsolete PlayerDataChanged event flag. Typed Direct/Relay session-lifecycle scenarios now exercise concurrent creation, reconnect, duplicate PlayerCreate delivery, identity takeover, entity-creation interruption, and final cleanup.

The old shared UI fixture can lose the headless widget transition. The v2 component-GUI action now has authoritative results, targeted duplicate/reorder coverage, late join, stable-identity reconnect and save/reload evidence in both transports.

The legacy Roslyn/UI commands omit current request identity and expected terrain revision and are correctly rejected by the authoritative server. The typed scenario drives ComponentMiner production inputs with authority and replay evidence.

The old sequential player fixture attacks a target after earlier UI steps have failed. The typed inventory-health scenario performs a real melee ray and verifies authoritative damage, revisions, observer state, respawn, faults, and reload.

The legacy aim script relies on shared UI and inventory state. The v2 scenario supplies real ComponentInput Aim and proves the PlayerAimPacket-to-projectile production chain, exactly-once observer events, lifecycle mutation, and reload boundaries.

The legacy editable-block scripts predate request identity, expected logic revision, structured authoritative state, and moving-block generations. The v2 logic scenario covers those contracts and rejects the obsolete mutations.

The old mount helper predates request identity and lifecycle/revision baselines. The typed mount scenario exercises production ComponentRider and Boat paths with range rejection, stale revisions, lifecycle replacement, disconnect, reconnect, and reload.
The legacy suicide path depends on a multi-dialog Clothing UI transition that is not reliable headlessly. No replacement is claimed: explicit choke/suicide UI coverage remains a planned feature gap.
